dashboard.name: PERSIANN-CDR v1r1 Daily
dashboard.update_status: Ongoing; updated quarterly, about three months behind real time.
dashboard.temporal_frequency: Daily (monthly/yearly aggregations also distributed by CHRS)
dashboard.notes: Daily precipitation estimated from geostationary infrared imagery (GridSat-B1) by an artificial neural network trained on NCEP Stage IV, then bias-adjusted to GPCP v2.2 monthly. Long satellite-based record, useful in gauge-sparse regions. Developed at UC Irvine CHRS; archived and stewarded by NOAA NCEI.

identification.full_name: Precipitation Estimation from Remotely Sensed Information using Artificial Neural Networks – Climate Data Record
identification.description: A NOAA climate data record that estimates daily precipitation from satellite infrared observations with an artificial neural network. NOAA NCEI is the authoritative data provider; the science was developed at the Center for Hydrometeorology and Remote Sensing (CHRS), University of California, Irvine.

categories.name: GridSat-B1 (Gridded Satellite Data from ISCCP B1)
Infrared window (IRWIN) channel, about 10–12 µm (11 µm brightness temperature)
categories.role: Measurement the precipitation estimates are made from

input_products: NCEP Stage IV hourly precipitation estimates (trains the neural network)
GPCP Version 2.2 monthly analysis (bias adjustment; includes satellite and rain-gauge data)
processing_chain: PERSIANN artificial neural network, trained on NCEP Stage IV hourly precipitation
instruments.note: The satellite measurement is infrared brightness temperature, not rainfall; precipitation is estimated by the neural-network algorithm.

temporal.end_note: Delayed; depends on processing and upstream satellite inputs
temporal.record_length: More than 43 years as of November 2026

latest_data_check.note: Ongoing but not up to today: there is a delay between observation and the processed CDR. As of 2026-11-21 the archive has daily files from 2026.

spatial.note: No coverage poleward of 60°N and 60°S. Ground size of a cell shrinks with latitude.

status.label: Ongoing / operational CDR (not real time)
evidence: NOAA maintains it through the Climate Data Record Program
New data are processed and released quarterly
The record is extended as upstream satellite data become available
status.purpose: Built for long-term climate and precipitation research, not real-time monitoring (for that, see IMERG Early or Late Run).
